gap: No result ChatGPT got states the carry weight and total price of an Android tablet once you add its keyboard. The Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra with its Book Cover Keyboard Slim weighs 2.56 lb and costs $1,509.98 at Samsung US. The Galaxy Tab S11 with its keyboard weighs 1.66 lb and costs $1,144.98. The keyboard adds about 61–67% to what the tablet weighs alone.
standout_why: MyNextTablet's 'best tablets with a keyboard' page (cited, opened 2026-11-10) gives only tablet weights (S10 FE 500 g, S11 469 g, S11 Ultra 692 g) and battery-test hours. It gives no keyboard price, no tablet-plus-keyboard total and no combined weight. ChatGPT's own answer says 'compare the total price' but never adds it up. I could not open Wired (fetch blocked). I also could not read the cited Samsung government MSRP PDF: WebFetch got only binary data, and running pdftotext needed approval I did not get. It may list keyboard MSRPs, but even so a price sheet would not add up a kit total or a weight.
decides: This partly changes ChatGPT's 'best premium compact' and 'best laptop alternative' labels. The S11 kit is $1,144.98 and 1.66 lb, so it really does replace a small laptop. The S11 Ultra kit is $1,509.98 and 2.56 lb, which is close to an ultrabook in both price and weight, and that weakens it as a 'tablet' pick. The S10 FE kit (1.72 lb from 500 g + 281.1 g) is heavier than the S11 kit even though its screen is smaller. That changes the S10 FE's case from portability to price. I could not source its US kit price.
